content:
incident-bot: INCIDENT OPENED: P1 - inference-serving brownout in us-west-2. Multiple pods entering CrashLoopBackOff after rapid autoscale. Pager sent to oncall.

oscar (oncall): I'm on it. Seeing increased 5xx and token latencies. Confirming scope.

maria (sre): Yep. Dashboards show autoscaler scaling from 8 -> 32 -> 6 nodes in ~7m. Pod restarts spiking during scale events.

ben (infra): Node flapping looks related to cloud autoscaler decisions + pod evictions. I see a handful of nodes with kernel logs showing nvidia-driver rebinds during startup.

priya (ml): On the model side, alerts show a lot of OOMs inside runtime containers: 
```
2026-03-15T10:03:22Z runtime: ERROR: CUDA error: out of memory (CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED)
stack: runtime/fwd.cpp:512
2026-03-15T10:03:23Z runtime: INFO: container restarting (OOM)
```

oscar (oncall): Quick checklist: are we seeing mixed GPU driver versions on newly provisioned nodes? That would explain immediate OOMs if device memory not available or driver loads fail.

ben (infra): Confirmed. New node pool images are picking up a newer NVIDIA runtime package from automated image updates. Old nodes are on nvidia-driver 525.x, new ones pulled 550.x. Some pods expect pinned drivers/kernels.

maria (sre): Autoscaler is aggressively scaling due to a burst of queued requests. But because pods restart while nodes join, we get constant churn -> crashloops -> pod restarts -> more HPA triggers -> thrash. Classic feedback loop.

priya (ml): To reduce impact we can route traffic to the smaller, stable model variant (cpu-fallback or a quantized model) while infra stabilizes. This will reduce latency but maintain availability.

eng-ops: Action plan proposal: 1) Pause autoscaling / set scaling stabilization window 2) Pin node image or roll back image updates 3) Cordon new nodes with mismatched drivers 4) Temporarily route traffic to fallback variant 5) Notify customers.

oscar (oncall): Doing step 1 now - patching cluster-autoscaler to increase cooldown and stabilization window.

ben (infra): Command I'm applying: 
```
kubectl -n kube-system patch deployment cluster-autoscaler --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/args/--scale-down-unneeded-time","value":"10m"},{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/args/--scale-down-unready-time","value":"20m"}]'
```

maria (sre): Setting HPA stabilization window too: 
```
kubectl patch hpa inference-runtime -n inference --patch '{"spec": {"behavior": {"scaleDown": {"stabilizationWindowSeconds": 600}}}}'
```

priya (ml): I'll publish a routing rule to route 60% traffic to cpu-fallback variant and 40% to primary, to reduce pressure. Pushing now.

eng-ops: Also disabling scale-to-zero for this deployment: removes a noisy cold-start pattern.

customer-ops: Notifying customers on status page: "We are experiencing degraded inference performance in US-WEST-2. Mitigations in progress." Draft posted.

oscar (oncall): Meanwhile, isolating bad nodes: listing nodes with mismatched drivers.

ben (infra): Command: 
```
kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep nvidia
# nodes with label image=autoupdate-2026-03-14 -> cordon
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-45-67
kubectl drain ip-10-0-45-67 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

maria (sre): For pods stuck CrashLoopBackOff, I'm increasing restart backoff to give the node time to fully initialize: 
```
kubectl patch deployment inference-runtime -n inference --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"terminationGracePeriodSeconds":120}}}}'
```

priya (ml): Rolling runtime image back to previously validated tag (v20260211-stable) for a quick win. Patching deployment now.

eng-ops: Patching ingress router to add circuit-breaker: drop requests when queue > 40 to avoid cascading.

maria (sre): Monitor: pod restarts have dropped 70% after stabilize window + cordon. Error rate still elevated but trending down.

oscar (oncall): Handoff note for next oncall (ben): I changed cluster-autoscaler args, HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds = 600, pinned runtime image to v20260211-stable, cordoned three nodes (ip-10-0-45-67, ip-10-0-46-12, ip-10-0-47-99) for manual repro later. Disabled scale-to-zero for inference namespace. Traffic partially routed to cpu-fallback. Investigations ongoing about image auto-update pipeline.

ben (infra): I'll follow up with the infra-image team to revert automated upgrade policy and add driver compatibility checks in the image-builder. Created issue: INFRA-3219.

priya (ml): Customer impact note: some customers saw increased latency and transient 5xxs for ~18 minutes during the thrash window. No data loss. I queued a regression check suite against the fallback model.

customer-ops: Updating status: "Incident: Degraded performance in US-WEST-2. Reduced error rate after mitigations. Followup investigation and permanent fix in progress. Estimated recovery: partial recovery achieved."

maria (sre): Temp mitigation successful. Next steps: 1) postmortem 2) tighten autoscaler->HPA damping heuristics 3) add driver-version gating in node rollout 4) add runtime health check that fails ready state if GPU driver not available (to avoid scheduling onto partially initialized node).

oscar (oncall): Marking incident as 'Mitigated' but not yet 'Resolved'. Assigning postmortem to priya + ben. I'll hand off pager to ben.

ben (infra): Taking the remainder. Leaving notes in the incident doc. Will coordinate with image builder and add unit tests for driver-mismatch detection.

priya (ml): Will run evals against the fallback routing and schedule a quality regression check overnight.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: severity -> P1->P2 (mitigated). Timeline logged.

eng-ops: Quick notes for postmortem:
- Trigger: sudden traffic burst + aggressive autoscaler settings.
- Underlying cause: node image auto-update introduced driver version mismatch.
- Effect: rapid scale-up/down -> pod restarts -> higher error rate (brownout).
- Immediate fix: increase scaling stabilization, cordon nodes, rollback runtime image, route to fallback variant.
- Long term: artifact gating, autoscaler damping, runtime readiness check for GPU driver.

customer-ops: Will follow up with affected customers with a short summary + link to postmortem when ready.

oscar (oncall): Final handoff: ben oncall. I'm signing out. (reacted with :white_check_mark:)

ben (infra): Acknowledged. I'll own the follow-ups and ensure INFRA-3219 gets prioritized. (reacted with :eyes:)

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: mitigation complete, monitoring for recurrence. Postmortem assigned.
